sections.title: Passage 1: Astronaut ice cream, anyone?
sections.html:
Freeze

(verb). turn or be turned into ice or another solid as a result of extreme cold.

ex: We'll freeze to death

significantly

(adverb). in a way that is large or important enough to have an effect on something or to be noticed

ex: Profits have increased significantly over the past few years.

transportation

(noun). a system for carrying people or goods from one place to another using vehicles, roads, etc.

ex: the safe transportation of used nuclear fuel

pharmaceutical

(adjective). relating to medicinal drugs, or their preparation, use, or sale

ex: The British pharmaceutical giant AstraZeneca employs about 5,000 people in the town

storage

(noun). the action or method of storing something for future use.

ex: The room lacked storage space

biological

(adjective). connected with the science of biology

ex: Eating is a biological necessity!

preserve

(verb). Retain (a condition or state of affairs)

ex: He wanted to protect her and preserve her innocence.

Chemist

(noun). an expert in chemistry; a person engaged in chemical research or experiments.

ex: Klaproth was the leading chemist of his time in Germany.

container

(noun). an object that can be used to hold or transport something.

ex: This container will take six litres.

Similarly

(adverb). in a similar way

ex: He was late and I similarly was delayed.

manuscript

(noun). A book, document, or piece of music written by hand

ex: Braille is especially useful in making single manuscript copies of books

preservation

(noun). the act of keeping something in its original state or in good condition

ex: The customs necessary for the preservation of the forests must remain in force

valuable

(adjective). Worth a great deal of money.

ex: These antiques are extremely valuable.

process

(noun). a series of actions that you take in order to achieve a result

ex: The process causes physical difficulty and effort.

sublimation

(noun). the act of directing your energy, especially sexual energy, to socially acceptable activities such as work, exercise, art, etc.

ex: It may be purified by sublimation

efficient

(adjective). effective with the least energy/manpower consumed

ex: The city's transport system is one of the most efficient in Europe.

technique

(noun). A way of carrying out a particular task,

ex: We learned some techniques for relieving stress.

bacteria

(noun). the simplest and smallest forms of life. Bacteria exist in large numbers in air, water and soil, and also in living and dead creatures and plants, and are often a cause of disease

ex: Bacteria were collected by centrifugation and washed with water

enzyme

(noun). a substance produced by a living organism which acts as a catalyst to bring about a specific biochemical reaction.

ex:Such an enzyme is the pepsin of the stomach of the higher animals

virtually

(adverb). nearly; almost.

ex: That's virtually impossible, Elise.

chamber

(noun). A large room used for formal or public events.

ex: Meetings of the council are held in the council chamber.

coil

(verb). to wind into a series of circles; to make something do this

Ex: Mist coiled around the tops of the hills.

refrigerator

(noun). a piece of electrical equipment in which food is kept cold so that it stays fresh

ex: Store fruit juice in the refrigerator.

compressor

(noun). a machine that compresses air or other gases

ex: The compressor may be driven by a steam engine or in any other convenient manner.

vapour

(noun). a mass of very small drops of liquid in the air

ex: The hollow glass tank contains hot mercury vapour.

condense

(verb). to change from a gas into a liquid; to make a gas change into a liquid

Ex: Steam condenses into water when it cools.

solid

(adjective). Firm and stable in shape; not liquid or fluid.

ex: a white rose on a solid blue background

infer

(verb). to reach an opinion or decide that something is true on the basis of information that is available

ex: You can infer the meaning of the word from the context of the rest of the sentence.

microorganism

(noun). A microscopic organism, especially a bacterium, virus, or fungus

Ex: GAS is a micro-organism that belongs to the same family of bacteria that causes MRSA.

composition

(noun). A creative work, especially a poem or piece of music.

ex: We cannot determine the chemical composition of soil simply by touching it.

altitude

(noun). the height of an object or point in relation to sea level or ground level.

ex: The plane lost altitude rapidly.

civilisation

(noun). a state of human society that is very developed and organized

ex: Some people think that nuclear war would mean the end of civilization.

peak

(noun). the pointed top of sth

Traffic reaches its peak between 8 and 9 in the morning.

pressure

(noun). Continuous physical force exerted on or against an object by something in contact with it.

ex: Let me check your blood pressure

freezer

(noun). a refrigerated compartment, cabinet, or room for preserving food at very low temperatures

ex: It's in the freezer, in a plastic bag wrapped with foil.

suspend

(verb). stop or delay sth for a time

ex: The ferry service has been suspended for the day because of bad weather.

animation

(noun). the state of being full of energy and enthusiasm.

ex: They used computer animation in the film.

revitalise

(verb). imbue (something) with new life and vitality

ex: It was thus his business to revitalize the old forms with a new and more vigorous content.

foodstuff

(noun). A substance suitable for consumption as food.

Ex: Even in Haflong, the markets are grappling to supply adequate foodstuffs

intact

(adjective). not damaged or impaired in any way; complete

ex: the church was almost in ruins but its tower remained intact

ripen

(verb). to become ripe

Ex: I'm waiting for the apples to ripen.

military

(adjective). Relating to or characteristic of soldiers or armed forces.

ex: There are sacrifices in any military campaign

cramped

(adjective). feeling or causing someone to feel uncomfortably confined or hemmed in by lack of space.

ex: His stomach cramped at the memory of that cliff.

spacecraft

(noun). a vehicle used for traveling in space

Ex: In 1993, Nasa's Observer spacecraft vanished three days before it was due to enter orbit

convert

(verb). Change the form, character, or function of something.

Ex: When you eat, your body converts food into glucose (blood sugar), which gives energy to your cells.’

molecule

(noun). A group of atoms bonded together,

ex: A molecule is made up of atoms.

liquid

(noun). a substance that flows freely and is not a solid or a gas, for example water or oil

ex: Mercury is a liquid at room temperature.

arc

(noun). A part of a curve, especially a part of the circumference of a circle.

Ex: This work attempted to solve the problem of constructing a line of the same length as an arc of a circle.

atmospheric

(adjective). relating to the atmosphere of the earth or (occasionally) another planet.

ex: They used an air compressor to take in atmospheric air , compress it, and force it into the cabin.

thaw

(verb). to turn back into water after being frozen

Ex: The country was slowly thawing out after the long cold winter.

molecular

(adjective). relating to or consisting of molecules.

ex: relating to or produced by or consisting of molecules

vacuum

(noun). a space that is completely empty of all substances, including all air or other gas

ex: the political vacuum left by the death of the Emperor

pump

(noun). a mechanical device using suction or pressure to raise or move liquids, compress gases, or force air into inflatable objects such as tires.

She washed her face at the pump in front of the inn.

frost

(noun). A deposit of small white ice crystals formed on the ground or other surfaces

Ex: If an unexpected frost occurs, undamaged fruits can be salvaged and ripened.

sufficiently

(adverb). enough for a particular purpose; as much as you need

ex: I was sufficiently close to hear what they were saying.

package

(noun). an object or group of objects wrapped in paper or plastic, or packed in a box

ex: There'll be a nice severance package for all of you

degrade

(verb). to show or treat somebody in a way that makes them seem not worth any respect or not worth taking seriously

Ex: This poster is offensive and degrades women.

restore

(verb). Bring back or re-establish

Ex: In order to facilitate subsistence economy, fishing and hunting rights were restored to the Inuit in 1980.

unscathed

(adjective). without suffering any injury, damage, or harm

Ex: All eight climbers were rescued unharmed.

concept

(noun). An abstract idea

ex: The concept of free speech is unknown to them.

sections.title: Passage 2: THE WILD SIDE OF TOWN
sections.html:
wildlife

(noun). Wild animals collectively; the native fauna (and sometimes flora) of a region.

ex: The wildlife out here depends on the water hole

ecosystem

(noun). a biological community of interacting organisms and their physical environment

ex: Pollution can have disastrous effects on the delicately balanced ecosystem.

ideal

(adjective). most suitable option for one’s desire/requirement

Ex:Therein lies the gap between ideal principle and business reality

fragmentation

(noun). the act or process of breaking or making something break into small pieces or parts

Ex: He claimed that social fragmentation was a by-product of the internet.

agrochemical

(noun). any chemical used in farming, especially for killing insects or for making plants grow better

Ex: Nevertheless, many agrochemical companies are undertaking extensive research programmes on biological control

lowland

(adjective). connected with an area of land that is fairly flat and not very high above sea level

Ex: These plants are mainly found in lowland areas/regions.

catastrophic

(adjective). Involving or causing sudden great damage

Ex: But sooner or later, a large object will threaten to hit the earth-moon system causing catastrophic damage.’

pesticide

(noun). A substance used for destroying insects or other organisms harmful to cultivated plants or to animals.

Ex: The synthetic pyrethroids are more stable than the pyrethrins, and are equally or more potent pesticides

revolution

(noun). a change in the way a country is governed, usually to a different political system and often using violence or war

ex: The country seems to be heading towards revolution.

intimate

(adjective). closely acquainted; familiar, close

Ex: He has an intimate knowledge of American literature

mosaic

(noun). a pattern or picture made using many small pieces of coloured stone or glass

Ex: The country is now a cultural and social mosaic (= mixture) due to the influx of different ethnic groups.

interconnect

(verb). to connect similar things; to be connected to or with similar things

Ex: The problems of poverty and unemployment are all interconnected.

hedge

(noun). a fence or boundary formed by closely growing bushes or shrubs

Ex: She kicked the ball so powerfully that it flew over the hedge.

habitat

(noun). The natural home or environment of an animal, plant, or other organism.

ex: Secondly, the wildlife has to compete with the surrounding agriculture for the habitat.

hedgerow

(noun). a line of bushes planted along the edge of a field or road

Ex: A hedgehog is any of the spiny mammals of the subfamily Erinaceinae, in the eulipotyphlan family Erinaceidae.

farmland

(noun). land that is used for farming

ex: In the past 18 years, the average price of Iowa farmland has increased 234 percent.

isolation

(noun). The process or fact of isolating or being isolated

ex: The prisoner had been kept in isolation for three days.

species

(noun). a group of living organism that are identical to each other

ex: Most of the known rhino species are West African

ecological

(adjective). Relating to or concerned with the relation of living organisms

ex: The destruction of the rain forests is an ecological disaster.

tangle

(noun). a twisted mass of threads, hair, etc. that cannot be easily separated

Ex: She pulled the tangle of wires out of the box.

canal

(noun). a long straight passage dug in the ground and filled with water for boats and ships to travel along; a smaller passage used for carrying water to fields, crops, etc.

ex: THat's the ear canal

railway

(noun). A track made of steel rails along which trains run.

ex: We live close to the railway line.

embankment

(noun). a wall of stone or earth made to keep water back or to carry a road or railway/railroad over low ground

ex: A bridge and an embankment connect it with Caprera.

verge

(noun). an edge or border

Ex:They're on the verge of bankruptcy

boundary

(noun). A line that marks the limits of an area; a dividing line.

ex: The Ural mountains mark the boundary between Europe and Asia.

lace

(verb). a fine open fabric, typically one of cotton or silk, made by looping, twisting, or knitting thread in patterns and used especially for trimming garments.

Ex: His hands shook as he fumbled to lace his boots

corridor

(noun). A long passage in a building from which doors lead into rooms

ex: She continued faster, and followed the corridor as it curved to the left.

hedgehog

(noun). a small brown animal with stiff parts like needles (called spines ) covering its back. Hedgehogs are nocturnal (= active mostly at night) and can roll into a ball to defend themselves when they are attacked.

Ex: The hedgehog curled up in a prickly ball

kingfisher

(noun). a bird with a long beak, that catches fish in rivers. The European kingfisher is small and brightly coloured and the American kingfisher is larger and blue-grey in colour.

Ex: Kingfishers or Alcedinidae are a family of small to medium-sized, brightly colored birds in the order Coraciiformes.

dragonfly

(noun). an insect with a long thin body, often brightly coloured, and two pairs of large transparent wings. Dragonflies are often seen over water.

Ex: Bright blue dragonflies hovered and darted in the reeds.

recreation

(noun). the action or process of creating something again

His favourite recreations are golf and playing Scrabble.

accommodate

(verb). Fit in with the wishes or needs of.

ex: The new policies fail to accommodate the disabled.

wasteland

(noun). an unused area of land that has become barren or overgrown

Ex: It was a desolate wasteland except for some grazing sheep.

significance

(noun). the importance of something, especially when this has an effect on what happens in the future

Ex: She couldn't grasp the full significance of what he had said.

eclipse

(verb). an obscuring of the light from one celestial body by the passage of another between it and the observer or between it and its source of illumination

Ex: The sun was partially eclipsed by the moon.

legacy

(noun). An amount of money or property left to someone in a will.

ex: An elderly cousin had left her a small legacy.

demolish

(verb). pull or knock down (a building)

Ex: The old factory was demolished to make way for a new parking lot

quarry

(noun). A large, deep pit, from which stone or other materials are or have been extracted.

Ex: Two stones at the quarry in 1884 weighed eighteen tons each.’

redundant

(adjective). without a job because there is no more work available

Ex: Her words always seem redundant to me, she repeats everything

brownfield

(noun). a former industrial or commercial site where future use is affected by real or perceived environmental contamination

Ex: Planners are committed to developing the city's brownfield sites before granting permission to build on the rural outskirts

so-called

(adjective). commonly designated by the name or term specified.

Ex: A so-called celebrity is looking for you.

spectacularly

(adverb). in a very impressive way

Ex: At night, the city is spectacularly lit.

colonize

(verb). (of a country or its citizens) send a group of settlers to (a place) and establish political control over it

The area was colonized by the Vikings.

birch

(noun). a slender, fast-growing tree that has thin bark (often peeling) and bears catkins. Birch trees grow chiefly in north temperate regions, some reaching the northern limit of tree growth

Ex: He sat in his short overcoat leaning against a birch tree

willow

(noun). a tree or shrub of temperate climates that typically has narrow leaves, bears catkins, and grows near water. Its pliant branches yield osiers for basketry, and its wood has various uses

Ex: Generalist predators, such as spiders, ants and ladybirds, occurred on the willows but were never observed attacking the eggs.

grassland

(noun). a large area of open land covered with wild grass

Ex: The lion adapted itself to dry, open grassland where a yellow coat was most effective.

shallow

(adjective). Of little depth.

ex: She told her children to stay in the shallow end (of the swimming pool).

wetland

(noun). connected with or existing in areas of wet land

Ex: The title Pantanal refers to a region of Brazil: the largest freshwater wetland in the world

consequence

(noun). A result or effect, commonly unpleasant

ex: I told the hairdresser to do what she wanted to my hair, and look at the consequences!

predator

(noun). An animal that naturally preys on others.

ex: he population of rabbits is controlled by natural predators.

abundance

(noun). A very large quantity of something.

ex: The unhealthy lagoons contain abundance of fish

domestic

(adjective). of or inside a particular country, household

ex: Tell him I locked down all missile strikes on domestic territory.

exotic

(adjective). originating in or characteristic of a distant foreign country.

Ex: He avidly collected exotic, fast cars.

nectar

(noun). a sugary fluid secreted by plants, especially within flowers to encourage pollination by insects and other animals. It is collected by bees to make into honey

The bees fly within a five mile radius to collect nectar.

thriving

(adjective). Prosperous and growing

Ex: The island has a thriving community and a rich and tragic history.

artificial

(adjective). made or produced to copy something natural; not real

ex: All things are artificial, for nature is the art of God.

absorb

(verb). take in water due to chemical or physical force

ex: I have enough acreage and cattle to absorb some of the loss

excess

(adjective). in addition to an amount that is necessary, usual or legal

Ex: Excess food is stored as fat.

canopy

(noun). An ornamental cloth covering hung or held up over something,

Ex: Trees arched over the road, forming a canopy of leaves.

intercept

(verb). to stop somebody/something that is going from one place to another from arriving

Ex: Reporters intercepted him as he tried to leave the hotel.

rainstorm

(noun). a heavy fall of rain

Ex: We drove for five hours through a rainstorm.

Sustainable

(adjective). Able to be maintained at a certain rate or level.

ex: sustainable definitions of good educational practice

drainage

(noun). the system of water or waste liquids flowing away from somewhere into the ground or down pipes

Ex: Bad drainage caused the land to be flooded

runoff

(noun). a second vote or competition that is held to find a winner because two people taking part in the first competition got the same result

Ex: She won 55% of the votes in the run-off.

reed

(noun). the draining away of water (or substances carried in it) from the surface of an area of land, a building or structure, etc.

Ex: The roof was highpitched and covered with straw, hay, reeds or tiles

scientific

(adjective). involving science

ex: The project has attracted considerable criticism from the scientific community (= from scientists).

recovery

(noun). a return to a normal state of health, mind, or strength.

ex: At last the economy is showing signs of recovery.

dependent

(adjective). contingent on or determined by.

You can't be dependent on your parents all your life.

restoration

(noun). the work of repairing and cleaning an old building, a painting, etc. so that its condition is as good as it originally was

Ex: The palace is closed for restoration.

scheme

(noun). A large-scale systematic plan or arrangement for attaining some particular object

ex: Under the current marking/mark scheme, you need 90 percent to get an A.

conservation

(noun). prevention of wasteful use of a resource

Ex: Road development in the area has been severely affected by the conservation programmes of the council.

essence

(noun). the most important quality or feature of something, that makes it what it is

ex: The essence of my car is that it takes me places I want to go

marginal

(adjective). small and not important

Ex: This is a marginal improvement on October.

reservoir

(noun). a natural or artificial lake where water is stored before it is taken by pipes to houses, etc.

Ex: Lake Baikal is the largest freshwater lake in the world

reserve

(noun). a supply of a commodity not needed for immediate use but available if required

ex: she trusted him without reserve

skylark

(noun). a small bird that sings while it flies high up in the sky

Ex: Look! That is a skylark!

toad

(noun). a tailless amphibian with a short stout body and short legs, typically having dry warty skin that can exude poison

ex: Toads have drier, lumpier skins than frogs and spend less time in the water.

reversal

(noun). a change to an opposite direction, position, or course of action.

ex: He demanded a reversal of the previous decision/policy.

burgeon

(verb). to begin to grow or develop rapidly

Ex: the city's suburbs have burgeoned, sprawling out from the center Từ Đồng Nghĩa:

deafening

(adjective). (of a noise) so loud as to make it impossible to hear anything else

Ex: the music reached a deafening crescendo

dawn

(noun). the time of day when light first appears

Ex: It's almost dawn.

familiarize

(verb). to learn about something or teach somebody about something, so that you/they start to understand it

Ex: You'll need time to familiarize yourself with our procedures.

hare

(noun). an animal like a large rabbit with very strong back legs, that can run very fast

ex: The hare is increasing rapidly, as well as the fox.

eagle

(noun). a large bird of prey (= a bird that kills other creatures for food) with a sharp curved beak and very good sight

Ex: The eagle has landed

deer

(noun). (con nai) an animal with long legs, that eats grass, leaves, etc. and can run fast. Most male deer have antlers (= horns shaped like branches). There are many types of deer.

Ex: A deer watched them from the trees.

woodland

(noun). an area of land that is covered with trees

ex: Some very rare and special plants grow in these woodlands.

lifeless

(adjective). Dead or apparently dead.

Ex: He was a vegetarian, as he couldn't stand the lifeless sight of a dead deer or fish

plausible

(adjective). eeming reasonable or probable >< unreasonable, improbable (không có khả năng)

Ex: She could find no plausible explanation for its disappearance

supplement

(verb). to add something to something in order to improve it or make it more complete

Ex: He supplements his income by giving private lessons.

embrace

(verb). Hold (someone) closely in one's arms

ex: He was about to embrace his friend, but Nicholas avoided him

Biodiversity

(noun). the existence of a large number of different kinds of animals and plants which make a balanced environment

Ex: The mining project threatens one of the world’s richest areas of biodiversity.

sections.title: Passage 3: Running on empty
sections.html:
fatigue

(noun). việc khó nhọc

ex: Perhaps it was fatigue from the long journey

exhaustion

(noun). kiệt sức

Ex: Exhaustion forced her to sleep through the night.

athlete

(noun). Vận động viên điền kinh, thể dục thể thao

Ex: In spite of being a mediocre athlete at best, Dean had thrived on sports.

originate

(verb). bắt nguồn

Ex: The disease is thought to have originated in the tropics.

Precise

(adjective). Chính xác

ex: That's why he has so many precise numbers

tire

(verb). làm mệt nhọc

Ex: Her legs were beginning to tire.

hypothesis

(noun). giả thuyết

ex: Several hypotheses for global warming have been suggested.

standard

(noun). tiêu chuẩn

ex: their restaurant offers a high standard of service

petrol

(noun). xăng dầu

ex: It's petrol engine

distress

(noun). phiền muộn

Ex: Caring for people experiencing mental distress is often complex and challenging.

spring from

(phrase). Là nguyên nhân của cái gì đó

Ex: His need to be liked obviously springs from a deep-rooted insecurity.

overtax

(verb). Bắt ai làm việc quá nhiều, đòi hỏi quá nhiều ở sức lực, của ai...

Ex: Take it easy. Don't overtax yourself.

emotional

(adjective). thiên cảm xúc

ex: My doctor said the problem was more emotional than physical.

essence

(noun). bản chất

ex: The essence of my car is that it takes me places I want to go

physiological

(adjective). sinh lý

Ex: Abuse can lead to both psychological and emotional problems.

subconscious

(adjective). tiềm thức

Ex: Many advertisements work at a subconscious level.

cue

(noun). gợi ý

ex: They started washing up, so that was our cue to leave the party.

brink

(noun). bờ vực

Ex: This woman could bring me to the brink of insanity.

sensation

(noun). Cảm giác/Cảm nhận

Ex: He felt a tingling sensation down his side

interpret

(verb). Diễn giải

ex: the evidence is difficult to interpret

governor

(noun). thống đốc

Ex: Governors from most of the 50 states will meet in Omaha this weekend.

athletic

(adjective). mang tính thể thao; năng động

ex: She looks very athletic

Puzzling

(adjective). đánh đố

Ex: The results obtained are sometimes puzzling, because it is.

paradox

(noun). nghịch lý

Ex: The paradox of science is that its success in understanding nature has created problems for its understanding of human nature.

accumulation

(noun). tích lũy

ex: Accumulations of sand can be formed by the action of waves on coastal beaches.

simulate

(verb). mô phỏng

ex: Computer software can be used to simulate conditions on the sea bed.

cyclist

(noun). Người đạp xe

Ex: Increasing the number of cyclists is a straightforward way of making cycling much safer.

sensor

(noun). Thiết bị cảm biến

Ex: This generates battery power for the lamp and there is a light sensor to detect whether it is dark enough to switch on.

nerve

(noun). dây thần kinh

ex: Her nerve began to frazzle.

impulse

(noun). Cảm hứng

Ex: He had a sudden impulse/urge to stand up and sing.

fibre

(noun). Vải sợi; Chất xơ

ex: The fibres are woven into fabric.

endurance

(noun). sức chịu đựng

Ex: He showed remarkable endurance throughout his illness.

pedal

(noun). bàn đạp

Ex: I couldn't reach the pedals on her bike.

compensate

(verb). đền bù

Ex: My issue is that he's compensating for his own missed childhood by appropriating other people's childhoods.

proportion

(noun). Tỷ lệ

ex: His ears were drawn out of proportion with his head.

sprint

(verb). tăng tốc

Ex: She wanted to sprint until her body gave out then wait for her death to come

strive

(verb). phấn đấu

Ex: I will strive to achieve individuality in every project we do.

Mythology

(noun). Thần thoại

Ex: Pilgrims are treated to plays enacted from stories of Hindu mythology, featuring the well known adventures of gods and heroes

exhausted

(adjective). mệt mỏi

Ex: She was exhausted but couldn't sleep

reserve

(noun). dự trữ

ex: she trusted him without reserve

theoretically

(adverb). về mặt lý thuyết

Ex: It is theoretically possible.

regulate

(verb). Điều tiết, quản lý

ex: Her mother strictly regulates how much TV she can watch.

catastrophic

(adjective). thảm khốc

Ex: A catastrophic storm made landfall on US soil.

limitation

(noun). sự giới hạn

ex: Despite her limitations as an actress, she was a great entertainer.

physical

(adjective). Thuộc về mặt vật lý, cơ thể

ex: We've got a few thousand kids in real danger of immediate, physical harm

symptom

(noun). triệu chứng

Ex: He's complaining of all the usual flu symptoms a high temperature, headache, and so on

dole

(noun). phần chia được

Ex: Young people on (= receiving) the dole are often bored and frustrated.

signal

(noun). tín hiệu

ex: When she gave (them) the signal, they all cheered.

determinant

(noun). phương thức

Ex: Soil and climate are the main determinants of how land is used.

strategy

(noun). A plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim

We need to devise an effective long-term strategy.

workout

(noun). tập thể dục

Ex: After my workout, I have a sauna.

accordingly

(adverb). theo đó

Ex: When we receive your instructions we will act accordingly.

spurt

(verb). bắn, phọt ra

ex: Blood was spurting out all over the place.

vigil

(noun). sự thức đêm

His parents kept a round-the-clock vigil at his bedside.

hoard

(verb). tích trữ

Ex: During the siege people began hoarding food and supplies.

genetically

(adverb). về mặt di truyền

Ex: The brain's response to pain is, at least in part, genetically determined.

emergency

(noun). Tình huống khẩn

Ex: How would disabled people escape in an emergency?

unbearable

(adjective). không thể chịu đựng được

Ex: The heat was becoming unbearable.

controversial

(adjective). gây tranh cãi

Ex: A controversial plan to build a new road has met with protests.

content

(noun). Nội dung

Ex: We've discussed the unusual form of the book now, what about the content?

critical

(adjective). mang tính phê phán

ex: The report is highly critical of safety standards at the factory.

marathon

(noun). đua đường dài

ex: She did/ran her first marathon in just under three hours.

norm

(noun). điều thuờng tình

Ex: One child per family is fast becoming the norm in some countries.

regulator

(noun). Bộ điều hòa

Ex: An extremely accurate clock, called a regulator, is used to measure the time it occurs

irrelevant

(adjective). không liên quan

ex: theory can sometimes be hastily dismissed as irrelevant to the classroom
